slides.title: CoRenew: A large language model agent-based policy simulation platform for multifamily residential redevelopment
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED POLICY SIMULATION FOR RESIDENTIAL REDEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: CoRenew utilizes LLM-based agents to simulate stakeholder negotiations and evaluate policy effects, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: CoRenew is an LLM-agent platform for simulating multi-round negotiations to evaluate multifamily residential redevelopment policies.
card.key_idea: It uses LLM-based resident agents structured by the Theory of Planned Behavior, rule-based planner/developer agents, and a representative-selection mechanism to simulate adaptive stakeholder responses to policies.
card.evaluation: Validated against 324 resident surveys (100% directional agreement) and a real-world 9-month negotiation case; tested via a Huadu District case study.

slides.title: Cocktail-Talker: Multi-Speaker Dialog Modeling in Noisy Social Environments with Turn Action GRPO
slides.tldr: MULTI-SPEAKER DIALOG MODELING IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for multi-speaker spoken dialog that determines whether to respond, listen, or ignore in noisy social settings. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Cocktail-Talker enables speech assistants to selectively respond, listen, or ignore in noisy multi-speaker environments.
card.key_idea: A Qwen2.5-Omni-based framework using three action tokens, trained via SFT and GRPO reinforcement learning on simulated multi-speaker dialogs from the Cocktail-DialogGen pipeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seen/unseen environments using binary Respond/Silent accuracy and response quality metrics (METEOR, ROUGE-L). Results show significant improvement over baseline speech LLMs.
card.limitation: The system is not streaming, assumes fixed turn boundaries, and lacks visual or spatial sensors for speaker inference.

slides.title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HUMAN TRUST AND INFLUENCE IN REPEATED HRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces the BAIT controller to manage the trade-off between long-term influence and human trust in repeated interactions, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: BAIT balances long-term influence and human trust to maintain robot task performance during repeated interactions.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical particle filter infers short-term strategies and long-term beliefs, feeding a belief-aware MPPI planner that optimizes the trade-off between unpredictability (influence) and transparency (trust).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations, a human-subject study, and real-world GEM vehicle lane-merging; BAIT matched influence-only baselines' performance while significantly increasing user trust.
card.limitation: The approach relies on a structured human model and requires a specific interaction zone to activate belief-shaping maneuvers.

slides.title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexGen to generate dialogues with scenario-adaptive turn-taking by calibrating LLM predictions against human preferences. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: The provided text contains only the title and author information for the DuplexGen paper.

slides.title: Extended Reality as a Mediation Layer for Situated Human Control in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.highlight: This research proposes using Extended Reality (XR) as a mediation layer to improve how humans understand and control robot autonomy in dynamic environments, supporting the RwB focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes using Extended Reality (XR) as a bidirectional mediation layer for situated human control in human-robot teaming.
card.key_idea: XR mediates between human intent and robot autonomy via four functions: grounding multimodal input, contextualizing plans for judgment, managing shared control levels, and coordinating team roles/recovery.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines a research agenda and suggests operational tests (e.g., measuring correction latency) rather than reporting experimental results.
card.limitation: The paper is a position piece providing a conceptual framework and design dimensions rather than a validated technical implementation.

slides.title: Let Me Look at You: Advanced Facial Expression Modeling for Conversational Speech Synthesis
slides.highlight: This work introduces FacialTalker and the VSDD-1K dataset to improve empathetic speech interaction through facial expression modeling, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: FacialTalker enhances conversational speech synthesis by integrating user facial expressions via a novel visual tokenizer.
card.key_idea: Uses AUTokenizer to discretize facial Action Units into single tokens and DualDPO to jointly optimize visual and speech preference constraints within an LLM backbone.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VSDD-1K, MultiDialog, and AvaMERG using objective metrics (F1, SIM, PDTW) and subjective MOS; outperformed strong baselines in naturalness and expressiveness.

slides.title: VISA: A Structured Description Protocol for Agent-Based Simulation Models Towards Machine Reproducibility
slides.tldr: STRUCTURED PROTOCOL FOR MACHINE-REPRODUCIBLE AGENT-BASED MODELS
slides.highlight: VISA introduces a symbol-based description protocol and LLM-executable skills to make agent-based models machine-parseable and unambiguous. This supports MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation by improving the reproducibility and transparency of agent models.

card.one_liner: VISA is a structured, symbol-based protocol using eight tables to make agent-based models machine-reproducible.
card.key_idea: A protocol specifying agent-level (Agent, Variable, Sensing, Internal Function) and model-level (Data, I/O, Schedule, Validation) tables, governed by 19 consistency rules for automated parsing and code generation.
card.evaluation: Validated on three external ABMs; successfully reproduced two cross-language (NetLogo to Python) and captured one industrial AnyLogic model, identifying specific proprietary blocks.
card.limitation: Reproduction can still be blocked by proprietary libraries or unavailable data, though VISA localizes these dependencies.

slides.title: AtmosERC: Modeling Dialogue-Level Affective Atmosphere for Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work introduces AtmosERC, a graph-based framework for emotion recognition in conversation that models dialogue-level affective atmosphere. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement through the estimation of latent emotional tendencies in dialogues.

card.one_liner: AtmosERC improves conversation emotion recognition by using a dialogue-level affective atmosphere as a global prior.
card.key_idea: It extracts a stable affective atmosphere vector via relation-aware graph filtering, which serves as a reusable prior to guide local utterance emotion decoding.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, EmoryNLP, and DailyDialog against sequence, graph, and LLM-based baselines; results show consistent improvements over global context pooling.
card.limitation: A gap exists between predicted atmosphere descriptors and gold-proxy dominant emotions, indicating room for better estimation and verbalization.

slides.title: Beyond Feeling Better: Capability-Sustaining Emotional Dialogue as a Longitudinal Research Paradigm
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a longitudinal research paradigm for emotional dialogue that focuses on sustaining user capacities for emotion regulation and social connection, contributing to HyECHO's goal of understanding engagement and social perception.

card.one_liner: Proposes CSED, a longitudinal paradigm for emotional dialogue that sustains user capabilities beyond immediate relief.
card.key_idea: CSED shifts the unit of inquiry to the full interaction lifecycle, integrating six design commitments (e.g., autonomy preservation, resilience activation) with a four-timescale evaluation framework.
card.evaluation: Conducted a PRISMA-ScR audit of 91 papers and function-coded 300 ESConv turns; found 95% of system-building papers focus solely on relief-oriented goals.
card.limitation: Relies on a sampled arXiv audit and AI-only coding; longitudinal measurement introduces privacy, surveillance, and selective attrition risks.

slides.title: Learning Social Robot Navigation By Sensing Human Legs
slides.tldr: SOCIAL ROBOT NAVIGATION VIA LEG SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces CALF, a neural architecture that interprets leg motion from LiDAR scans to improve social compliance in robot navigation, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: CALF enables socially compliant robot navigation by interpreting human leg dynamics from 2D LiDAR scans.
card.key_idea: A hybrid neural architecture combining 1D-CNNs, temporal self-attention, and MLP, trained via DRL in a custom simulator (LegNav) featuring a realistic Non-Slip Gait model.
card.evaluation: Compared against classical and RL baselines in simulation and validated via zero-shot deployment on a TurtleBot 4 using navigation and social compliance metrics.

slides.title: Solitics Launches Saai for Retail Banking Customer Engagement
slides.highlight: The launch of Saai for automating customer engagement provides insights into agentic AI's role in managing interactions, relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

slides.title: When Robots Exchange Meaning: A Demo of Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications for Collaborative Robotics
slides.highlight: This work presents a semantic communication testbed that reduces visual data payload for 3D mapping and object handling, supporting the embodied AI and interaction goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: A robot-edge testbed demonstrating goal-oriented semantic communication for collaborative robotics using VQ-VAE visual compression.
card.key_idea: RGB frames are encoded into VQ-VAE tokens on-robot, reconstructed at the edge, and integrated with RTAB-Map and YOLO for semantic 3D mapping and mission control.
card.evaluation: Offline tests showed 21.7–21.9 dB PSNR and a 42.67x reduction in model-input RGB bytes. Results are presented as a proof-of-concept demo.
card.limitation: Detailed runtime comparisons, wireless latency characterization over 5G/Open RAN, and energy consumption analysis are not yet provided.
